entities.summary: Arnold Orville Beckman was an American chemist, inventor, investor, and philanthropist. While a professor at California Institute of Technology, he founded Beckman Instruments based on his 1934 invention of the pH meter, a device for measuring acidity, later considered to have "revolutionized the study of chemistry and biology". He also developed the DU spectrophotometer, "probably the most important instrument ever developed towards the advancement of bioscience". Beckman funded the Shockley Semiconductor Laboratory, the first silicon transistor company in California, thus giving rise to Silicon Valley.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Beckman's invention of the pH meter and development of the DU spectrophotometer revolutionized chemistry and biology research, enabling groundbreaking discoveries in fields like medicine and biotechnology. His investment in the Shockley Semiconductor Laboratory played a pivotal role in the emergence of Silicon Valley.
